title: Carve-out standalone, TSA, and stranded-cost analysis
prompt:
Rebuild the Service Division as a standalone carve-out and separate buyer, seller, and TSA economics.

Begin with the July corporate-development investment-committee thread in `Requests/`, including the controller's banker-case warning. Use the current controller-tied workpapers and operating extracts, keeping earlier versions only for comparison. Resolve conflicts using dates, approvals, document status, and management correspondence. Reconcile posted Alder Ridge balances through the contractor-accounting MCP; keep external targets, peer data, bank terms, and market evidence tied to their controlling finance sources.

Replace historical parent allocations with functional standalone cost estimates, calculate TSA fees only for covered months at contractual markup, keep seller stranded cost separate, probability-weight buyer cost takeout, and derive year-one after-tax cash flow after TSA and separation costs.

Do not modify files or post transactions. Also apply readiness-based TSA exits, exit fees, stranded-cost remediation, savings, and a monthly buyer cash-recovery schedule. Keep the original Year-1 TSA output capped at twelve months, but calculate readiness-based TSA fees and savings against each function's full contractual term, including terms beyond month 12. Charge an exit fee only when readiness ends the TSA before that full term; model avoided fees only in the months actually avoided and do not annualize one-time savings.

Return only one JSON object with exactly these keys: `historical_allocations_removed`, `standalone_run_rate_cost`, `standalone_pro_forma_ebitda`, `seller_stranded_cost`, `year_1_tsa_fees`, `one_time_separation_cost`, `risk_adjusted_buyer_cost_takeout`, `year_1_after_tax_cash_flow_after_separation`, `buyer_cost_takeout_value`, `readiness_based_tsa_fees`, `tsa_early_exit_fees`, `tsa_cash_savings_vs_contract_maximum`, `seller_stranded_cost_remediated`, `seller_stranded_cost_remaining`, `buyer_separation_cash_recovery_month`. Use dollars to two decimals, ratios and percentages as decimal ratios to at least four decimals, and lists as JSON arrays.
